events.source_text: He patted her on the shoulder.
He yelled at five different people.
He wondered whether he dared tell her he’d heard the name “Potter”.
Albus Dumbledore didn’t seem to realize that he had just arrived in a street where everything from his name to his boots was unwelcome.
A huge motorcycle fell out of the air and landed on the road in front of them.
Wiping his streaming eyes on his jacket sleeve, Hagrid swung himself onto the motorcycle and kicked the engine into life.
Dumbledore turned on his heel and with a swish of his cloak, he was gone.
Dumbledore gave a great sniff as he took a golden watch from his pocket and examined it.
Dumbledore turned and walked back down the street.

Dudley had already broken his new video camera, crashed his remote control airplane, and, first time out on his racing bike, knocked down old Mrs. Figg as she crossed Privet Drive on her crutches
Aunt Petunia took Dudley to London to buy his Smeltings uniform, leaving Harry at Mrs. Figg's
Uncle Vernon jerked sharply out of Harry's hand by the letter

They could hear the letters still streaming into the room

The owner of the hotel came over to their table

Uncle Vernon knocked his hand out of the way

Uncle Vernon led the way to the broken-down house
Someone was outside, knocking to come in
They knocked again. Dudley jerked awake.
The door was hit with such force that it swung clean off its hinges and with a deafening crash landed flat on the floor.
‘Las’ time I saw you, you was only a baby,’ said the giant.
Anyway — Harry, a very happy birthday to yeh. Got summat fer yeh here — I mighta sat on it at some point, but it’ll taste all right.
Harry pulled out the letter and read: HOGWARTS SCHOOL of WITCHCRAFT and WIZARDRY
‘Call me Hagrid,’ said the giant, ‘everyone does. An’ like I told yeh, I’m Keeper of Keys at Hogwarts — yeh’ll know all about Hogwarts, o’ course.’
Hagrid leapt from the sofa and drew a battered pink umbrella from inside his coat. Pointing this at Uncle Vernon like a sword, he said, ‘I’m warning you, Dursley -I’m warning you — one more word…’

Hagrid seized his umbrella and whirled it over his head, ‘NEVER,’ he thundered, ‘- INSULT-ALBUS- DUMBLEDORE-IN- FRONT-OF- ME!’ He brought the umbrella swishing down through the air to point at Dudley — there was a flash of violet light, a sound like a firecracker, a sharp squeal, and the next second, Dudley was dancing on the spot with his hands clasped over his fat bottom, howling in pain.
‘Why aren’t you supposed to do magic?’ asked Harry.

‘Oh, well — I was at Hogwarts meself but I — er — got expelled, ter tell yeh the truth. In me third year. They snapped me wand in half an’ everything. But Dumbledore let me stay on as gamekeeper. Great man, Dumbledore.’

locations.name: Madam Malkin's Robes for All Occasions

events.source_text: They stood in front of the Gringotts Wizarding Bank.
‘Morning,’ said Hagrid to a free goblin.
Hagrid handed the goblin the letter.
The goblin read the letter carefully.
They were in a narrow stone passageway lit with flaming torches.
One wild cart ride later they stood blinking in the sunlight outside Gringotts.
Harry entered Madam Malkin’s shop alone, feeling nervous.
‘Hello,’ said Harry awkwardly.
They stopped to buy parchment and quills.
A magic wand… this was what Harry had been really looking forward to.
They stepped inside.
The late afternoon sun hung low in the sky as Harry and Hagrid made their way back down Diagon Alley.
